question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The passages on offer and opt-out provide a window to opt out, but do not set a separate acceptance/decline deadline tied to notification.

* An officer/employee who is offered employment in the Institute “may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute” [629/2025 §33]; [621/2025 §33]; [551/2024 §33]

Caveats: The text gives the six-month opt-out period measured from the date the employment is offered, not an explicit time limit for deciding after notification of the offer, and no distinct deadline for accepting the offer is stated.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The amended Act defines “Director-General” as the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department appointed or deemed to have been appointed under the Act.

* “‘Director-General’ means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act;” [494/2024 §6]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment to s.6 of the Judicature Act changes the ages in s.6(3) and s.6(4).

* s.6(3): “sixty-one years” is substituted with “sixty-three years” [058/2026 §3]
* s.6(4) is replaced with: “Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355), the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years.” [058/2026 §3]
